snippet.title: 10 Things to NEVER Do as a Dementia Caregiver
snippet.description:
📞 Ready for concierge level support? Work with Dr. Sinclair by scheduling your call here: https://www.confidentcaregiveracademy.com/schedule
📥 New to Caregiving? Download the Free Care Starter Kit →https://www.confidentcaregiveracademy.com/confident-care-starter-kit-5steps-to-dementia-care

If you’re caring for someone with dementia, there are 10 things you should never do, not because you’re doing anything wrong, but because the dementia brain can’t process the world the same way anymore. These 10 common habits (that almost every caregiver unconsciously does) can make behaviors worse, increase arguing, and leave you feeling exhausted and defeated.

In this video, neuropsychologist and dementia care specialist Dr. Camille Sinclair walks you through the 10 things to avoid, why they backfire in the dementia brain, and exactly what to do instead.

You’ll learn the brain science behind arguing, repetition, refusal, and emotional outbursts, explained in a simple, compassionate way meant for real-life family caregivers.

Whether you’re new to dementia caregiving or years into the journey, these 10 shifts will help you:
Reduce arguing and defensiveness
Stop triggering confusion and overwhelm
Communicate more effectively
Calm tense situations
Build connection even when memory is fading
Understand what behaviors actually mean

You deserve to feel confident and supported, and this video gives you essential tools to create calmer, easier days with your loved one.

👉 If you want personalized support, book a free dementia caregiver consultation and see if you're a fit for the Confident Caregiver Academy: https://www.confidentcaregiveracademy.com/schedule
